chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Philadelphia job ends when the building is torn down; the Bronx apartment since 1940
summary: The Philadelphia club was sold and torn down; he had commuted home every Sunday to the same Bronx apartment he had lived in since 1940, rats and all.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: you know? What caused you to leave Philadelphia?

Ah, oh, well there was the -- they tore down -- they sold it out and tore down the building, tore down the -- I haven't been through there since then. I can imagine now it's all parking lots, or it has been for a heck of a long time.
I don't know what it looks like.
What did you do? Come back to New York?
Yeah, well I was living -- I was living -- still living at home.
You worked three years in Philadelphia, but you still lived in New York?
Oh, yeah. I used to come home every Sunday.
Used to come home every Sunday.
Where did you live then, in New York?
Same place, 76 and Trenton Avenue, for 34 years, in this same apartment.
Thirty-four years, that was what? 1940 you moved here?
1940. I knew -- I could shake hands
with all the rats. We knew each other by name, you know, and --
-- roaches would look at me and say aah, to hell with you. You know what I mean. And we -- so we had a ball then.
